scope: The new browser entry-point hook closes the demonstrated local-list/local-read gap in the pinned IDBFS flush.
Initial hydration delegates to the original native implementation. No retries, storage-error exemptions or renderer changes are introduced by this fix.
The archived DPR2 anonymous errno44 has no failing path/direction; this reproduction does not attribute that historical failure or change its failed quality outcome.
The controlled helper test is not an end-to-end browser persistence test. Fresh browser startup, persistence and full native quality remain pending on the actual published production build.

The unchanged IDBFS object is extracted from the explicitly supplied built native runtime and bound to the pinned helper hash. Only syncfs is wrapped for the proposed flush experiment; all original helper functions are retained.

The controlled filesystem and asynchronous IndexedDB doubles demonstrate the local-snapshot-to-read race. This is not a browser run and does not identify the cause of the observed anonymous errno 44 in CI.
The remote-first flush takes its local snapshot and invokes reconcile in the same JavaScript turn. Every loadLocalEntry and put argument capture for that flush is synchronous in that turn.

No retry, scheduling delay, fallback or error exemption is added. Errors retain object identity. After all queued events drain, each tested invocation has exactly one callback; error callbacks may precede transaction completion.

Request-error, transaction-error and abort notifications in the write-failure scenario are controlled fault injection. They test the native once-only error guard, not real IndexedDB request-error cancellation or abort behavior.

The deliberate enumeration-order change can alter which error is reported first if remote and local enumeration independently fail; this test preserves each individual operation error without suppressing it.
populate=true delegates to the original syncfs and preserves initial hydration data, timestamps, modes, error behavior and event order.

Mutations after put argument capture are outside that flush snapshot and still require a later synchronization. The test double verifies structured-clone byte isolation but does not qualify a production IndexedDB implementation.

findings.subject: Managed startup observes the exported native IDBFS object
findings.finding: RuntimeReady synchronously configures globalThis.IDBFS from Module.IDBFS before dependency initialization can call mainInit and managed Main. Program installs the wrapper before renderer diagnostics, host creation or App construction. Uno Runtime InvokeJS evaluates the expression and returns its result string.

findings.subject: Mounts dispatch through the same object after installation
findings.source: dotnet.native.wx7z35yrz9.js FS.mount and FS.syncfs; Uno.Wasm.js lines2045–2075
findings.finding: FS.mount stores the supplied IDBFS object as mount.type; FS.syncfs looks up mount.type.syncfs at dispatch time. Existing and later mounts therefore observe the replacement. StorageFolder.makePersistent awaits CoreApplication initialization and then mounts the exported IDBFS object.

findings.subject: Flush source enumeration and local reads share one synchronous JavaScript turn
findings.source: Exact native getLocalSet, loadLocalEntry, reconcile, storeRemoteEntry; UnoDraw.csproj WasmEnableThreads=false
findings.finding: getRemoteSet waits for IndexedDB cursor callbacks. For populate=false, the wrapper enumerates that remote set first, then runs synchronous local traversal and synchronous local reads initiated by reconcile before yielding. Each store.put is initiated from the same turn. This removes the source-proven rename/delete opportunity between the local filename snapshot and its reads in this pinned single-threaded runtime.

findings.subject: Original hydration, transactions, reconciliation and errors are retained
findings.source: BrowserStorageSynchronization.js and exact native IDBFS object
findings.finding: Truthy populate delegates directly to the original syncfs. Flush still calls the exact original getRemoteSet/getLocalSet/reconcile methods with original sets and callback, preserving create ordering, reverse removal ordering, mtime comparison, file bytes/modes/timestamps and IndexedDB transaction completion. Errors are forwarded without filtering or remapping. No retry, delay, extra flush or replacement transaction is introduced.

findings.subject: Installer lifetime and compatibility guards
findings.finding: The native object is a normal mutable object literal. The installer verifies the four methods, extensibility and writable own syncfs property, records one wrapper under a Symbol marker, and detects repeated installation or a later competing replacement. Unsupported objects retain their original behavior with a visible informational status.

observed_failure_attribution.reason: The archived error lacks the missing path/stack. Reproducing a valid rename/delete interleaving cannot identify the historical failing path.

limits: Applies to the exact pinned native IDBFS implementation and single-threaded application; function presence alone is not a proof for future changed runtime semantics.
The existing FS.syncfs first-error callback may precede other mounts; this draft deliberately does not retry or alter that behavior.
Cross-tab synchronization and page-close durability retain their existing runtime semantics.
The complete archived 0ffa quality run remains failed; this source review cannot relabel it or supply fresh browser qualification.

semantic_review: The original native IDBFS object is extracted unchanged with an exact helper hash; only the actual production installer replaces syncfs.

Cursor requests and database opening remain asynchronous controlled events; mutations occur in the gap after the original local snapshot. The corrected source enumeration and every local lookup happen in the same event turn.
put arguments are structured-cloned when enqueued; persistence publishes staged bytes only at the controlled transaction completion, and later local mutation cannot change captured bytes.
Hydration delegates to the original function and uses the same native helper path. Mode, timestamp, binary contents, source/removal ordering and error object assertions remain intact.

The injected request+transaction error/abort notifications stress the native once-only callback guard. They are explicitly scoped as fault injection rather than a model of browser cancellation after preventDefault.

The corrected report wording says counts are checked after the queue drains; error callbacks may precede transaction completion. Different independent simultaneous errors can change first-error priority when enumeration order changes.
limits: No browser or runtime test was rerun by this reviewer. The performance agent owns the actual controlled executions.
This evidence validates the demonstrated ordering invariant in the pinned source. It does not identify the historical anonymous errno44 path or qualify browser IndexedDB persistence.
The old full SVG result remains failed; no pixel, runtime-error or default-promotion gate is relaxed.

api_compile.scope: Exact new C# initialization class against actual Uno assemblies, with actual JavaScript embedded bytes; not a complete browser-app build.
